rounds.proof_sketch: N=4096, BLOCK_SIZE=16 → grid_dim=(256,256). col = bx*16 + tx where bx∈[0,255], tx∈[0,15]. Maximum col = 255*16+15 = 4095 = N-1. Since col_max < N, the condition 'col < N' is always true, and 'col <= N' is also always true. The mutation never changes behavior because col=N is unreachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the guard from 'col < N' to 'col <= N' for B tile loading. For N=4096 with BLOCK_SIZE=16, the grid dimensions are exactly 256×256 blocks. Each thread computes col = bx*BLOCK_SIZE + tx, giving a maximum value of 255*16+15=4095. Since 4096 is perfectly divisible by 16, there are no 'overflow' threads where col≥N. Therefore, the original condition 'col < N' (always true since col_max=4095<4096) and mutated condition 'col <= N' (always true since 4095≤4096) are semantically equivalent for all reachable thread configurations.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation would only manifest if col could equal N, which requires N % BLOCK_SIZE ≠ 0. With N=4096 and BLOCK_SIZE=16, the division is exact (4096/16=256), so no thread ever has col=N. A value-level test cannot change thread indexing; only a different matrix dimension (not permitted by contract) could expose this mutation.
rounds.recommendations: When testing relational operator mutations in CUDA kernels with tiled algorithms, pay special attention to whether the fixed dimensions are exact multiples of tile sizes. Boundary mutations in tile loading guards are only killable when there exist 'boundary' threads (i.e., when N % BLOCK_SIZE ≠ 0). For complete mutation coverage, test configurations should include dimensions that are NOT multiples of the tile/block size.
